rationales.explanation: Charles asks how the hotspot is activated and kept off, probing the operating and usage model.
Charles states the impression that satellite data may be prohibitively expensive to access, expressing an economics concern.
Charles probes whether the product provides a full hotspot experience, including high-bandwidth use cases.
Charles asks what Space 2.0 means and when the described future state will occur, probing timing.
Charles identifies the product as resembling an EPIRB, probing similarity to an existing solution without stating a negative conclusion.
Charles asks how Somewear compares with goTenna and whether the competing functionality also depends on line of sight.
Charles endorses the question about renting the device, continuing the probe of the business model.
Charles says he expects customers to sign up for annual plans and that the company will be fine on that point.
Charles accepts that there is an eventual opportunity to reach six-digit user scale.
Charles explicitly links his pass decision to lacking confidence in the company's growth velocity and the time required to reach the projected scale.

annotation_summary: Charles passes despite accepting the annual-plan model and eventual market opportunity; his explicit concern is uncertainty about the velocity and timing of customer-scale growth.
